title: Bulkhead

validation.research: Eight primary references: Michael Nygard’s Release It! publisher catalog establishes Bulkheads as a stability pattern; Microsoft describes resource/consumer pool partitioning and containment; AWS explains latency-driven concurrency overload and hard/soft dependency allocation; Resilience4j distinguishes semaphore admission on caller threads from fixed thread-pool execution with bounded queues; Python documents the actual semaphore, event and thread operations; Airflow describes task-slot admission; Snowflake establishes independent compute over shared persistent data; BigQuery distinguishes assigned capacity from borrowed idle capacity. Bulkhead is the established title and Bulkheads the catalog plural. The earlier Workload Isolation title is retained as an alias and described as an application. Cell-based deployment is broader than the teaching semaphore, which supplies no process, security or data boundary. The backfill/live scenarios, fixed 12/4/4 allowance, event-gated code and native illustrations are original teaching material.

runnable_example.verification: Actual article fences run unchanged on Python 3.11+. Exact four-line demo output. Real simultaneous ten-thread contention admits exactly three held actions and rejects seven; independent live compartment remains usable. Rejections never invoke callbacks or release unowned permits. Successful/falsy returns, non-callable actions, ValueError, TypeError and cancellation-like BaseException preserve result/error identity and return capacity. Callbacks execute on their caller threads. An actual TemporaryFile remains open during gated finally cleanup; stopping an observer wait does not free capacity, and cleanup closes the file before result observation. Capacity-one reentry refuses immediately, later calls reuse capacity, and all owned threads are released and joined. No queue, fairness, CPU or byte reservation, timeout, action termination, async completion, fleet-wide cap or shared-data synchronization is inferred.

example_limits: Existing canonical data-workload-isolation explicitly taught a Bulkhead application and is revised in place, retaining ID/URL, Data Engineering tags/verse, original allocation-figure path, backfill/live problem, fixed 12/4/4 worker allowance, Airflow admission, Snowflake compute separation, BigQuery borrowing caveat and historical import provenance. Established Bulkhead becomes the title; Bulkheads and former title Workload Isolation are aliases, with workload isolation described as an application rather than a promise of universal isolation. Its one primary home moves to Reliability and Failure Handling; Execution & recovery retains a cross-link and twelve remaining members. Original article/SVG are archived locally. Original Python 3.11+ Bulkhead uses a retained BoundedSemaphore per compartment, positive integer capacity rejecting Boolean values, nonblocking admission and finally-based release around a zero-argument synchronous action. A separate owned event-gated thread holds backfill’s one permit, a second backfill is rejected without invocation, and live runs on its own available caller thread using an independent permit. Release and join precede re-admission. The gate does not create/reserve threads, queue, impose deadlines, cancel actions, coordinate the fleet, bound bytes/rate, isolate callback shared state or establish data correctness. Actions own resource cleanup and must not return unfinished work. Verified with real semaphores and owned threads, including exact output, ten simultaneous callers at capacity three, independent live admission, rejection without invocation, error identity, callback-owned TemporaryFile cleanup lifetime and reentry. Test watchdogs only bound verification waits. No real network service, scheduler, CPU isolation, cancellation, fleet-wide coordination or thread reservation is inferred.
